interpretation.success: Conditional on a new alert starting within five hours of leak onset, localization is extremely strong on Net1: the true node is top-three in all 29 early-detected events and top-one in 28 of 29.
interpretation.failure: Only 29 of 55 leak events start a qualifying alert in the first five hours. Detection/alert onset, not localization, is the dominant end-to-end bottleneck. Later alerts raise eventual detection to 87.3% but localization quality falls because they are farther from the hydraulic transition and can represent unrelated alert episodes.
interpretation.operational_reading: The current system can narrow a nine-node search space well once it recognizes the event, but it is not yet reliable enough to serve as a stand-alone early dispatch trigger.
interpretation.next_iteration: Diagnose early missed events against the frozen detector probabilities and build a two-stage onset policy that preserves challenge-005 nuisance limits while increasing new-alert starts in the first ten half-hour steps. Keep the localizer frozen for the next end-to-end test.
